questions.question: Which of the following is a good, strong password?
choices: A series of numbers, letters, and special characters that you can remember
questions.explanation: A strong password should be difficult to guess but easy to remember. Include numbers and symbols, and remember that longer passwords are stronger.

questions.question: Who should you share your password with?
questions.explanation: Never share your passwords with anyone except trusted adults like your parents.

questions.question: When browsing the internet, you should avoid which of the following?
choices: Downloading files from a website you're not familiar with
Reading articles on things you're interested in
questions.explanation: Always be careful downloading files online, and ensure the place you're downloading from is safe and trustworthy.

questions.question: Where is a safe place to download apps?
choices: The official app store on your device
A site you were recommended by a friend
Something you were recommended by an ad
It's not safe to download any apps, stick with what you have
questions.explanation: While not every app outside the app store is unsafe, generally you should stick to apps that have been approved by the official app store your device uses to stay secure.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help keep your device secure?
choices: Logging out of your device when you aren't using it
Writing down your password so you remember it
questions.explanation: It's generally not a good idea to write down passwords, as others might read them and figure out what your password is.

questions.question: Which of the following helps add extra security to your device?
choices: Never turn on WiFi on your device
Turn on auto fill for your passwords
questions.explanation: Two-factor authentication adds an extra method of verifying your identity on top of a password and helps keep your device extra secure.

questions.question: Which of the following should you be careful connecting to?
choices: A public WiFi router at a restaurant
questions.explanation: You should always be careful connecting to networks you don't recognize, as many are insecure and can expose your device to danger.

questions.question: What is the process of making data unreadable by humans to protect it called?
questions.explanation: Encryption uses mathematical processes to turn readable text and data into unreadable strings of characters so it stays protected while being sent.

questions.question: What should you do when you're done using a public computer on your account?
questions.explanation: Always log out of all your accounts when you're done using public computers, as anyone can sit down and gain access to your account if you don't.

questions.question: What should you do when your device is not currently using WiFi or Bluetooth?
choices: Shut your device down and don't use it
Leave WiFi or Bluetooth on all the time
Turn off WiFi or Bluetooth when they aren't being used
questions.explanation: Leaving Bluetooth and WiFi on while you're not using them can expose your device to threats, so turn them off when they're not being used.

questions.question: If you have to leave your computer alone while in public, make sure you __ before walking away.
choices: Close all your tabs and apps
Log out and turn it off or close it
questions.explanation: You should try to avoid leaving your computer alone out in public, but if you have to walk away for a few minutes for some reason, make sure to log out and turn off the computer so no one can access your account.

questions.question: Which of these passwords is most secure?
questions.explanation: A strong password should be difficult to guess but easy to remember. Include lots of numbers and symbols, and longer is stronger!

questions.question: Two factor authentication is useful for what?
choices: Keeping your device safe even if you password is stolen
Keeping people from guessing your password
Making it harder to log in to your device
questions.explanation: Two Factor authentication adds an extra method of verifying your identity on top of a password, and helps keep your device extra secure.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT dangerous to do online.
choices: Write your password in a message
Download Files from somewhere you don't recognize
Make an account password something simple
questions.explanation: Always be careful downloading files online, and make sure your personal information and passwords are secure and private.

questions.explanation: A strong password should be difficult to guess but easy to remember. Include lots of numbers and symbols, and longer is stronger!

questions.question: Always ___ before leaving a public computer.
questions.explanation: Always log out of all your accounts when you're done using public computers, as anyone can sit down and gain access to your account if you don't.

questions.question: If you're not using ___ you should turn it off.
questions.explanation: Leaving on Bluetooth, WiFi, and NFC while you're not using them can expose your device to threats, ensure you turn them off when they're not being used.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a useful security method for your mobile device?
questions.explanation: While some large computers can be protected with physical security like locks, they're not practical for your mobile device.

questions.question: Which of these passwords is most secure?
questions.explanation: A strong password should be difficult to guess but easy to remember. Include lots of numbers and symbols, and longer is stronger!

questions.question: A ___ is a security tool that protects your device by hiding your real IP address
questions.explanation: A VPN is a security tool that protects your device by hiding your real IP address, creating an encrypted "tunnel" between you and the things you connect to.

questions.question: If an app asks you for permissions and you're not sure why, what should you do?
choices: Give it the permissions and hope it's ok
Deny the permissions until you can figure out if the app is trustworthy
Uninstall immediately and tell all your friends it's unsafe
questions.explanation: If an app asks for permissions to access something it doesn't seem like it should need, it's best to try to understand why it's asking and verify that the app is safe before allowing it access.

questions.question: ___ is the process of turning readable text into something unreadable by humans for secure transmission
questions.explanation: Encryption uses math equations to turn readable text and data into random strings of numbers and letters humans can't read to protect it while it's being sent.

questions.question: If your friend asks for your password, what should you do?
choices: Tell them no and explain that you shouldn't share passwords
questions.explanation: Never share your passwords with anyone except trusted adults like your parents.

questions.question: All of the following are a type of device security except ___.
questions.explanation: A hard drive is the physical data storage device in your computer it doesn't keep anything secure on it's own.

questions.question: It's important to ___ regularly to have the best possible device security.
questions.explanation: Changing your password regularly is a good way to maintain extra security.
